targets.name: job-store
targets.rationale: Job state transitions back long-running route behavior and must not silently regress. The target's witness command follows the implementation boundary by combining the store and lifecycle contract suites. Exclusions are limited to syntax-only postponed annotations, a private keyword marker, a non-negative-depth comparison equivalence, and deliberately non-contractual numeric rank magnitudes; executable lifecycle decisions remain mutation-tested.

targets.name: path-resolution
targets.rationale: Path validation is a security boundary; mutation survivors are treated as high-priority signal.

targets.name: registry
targets.rationale: Registry contracts define node/API surface area and should be resistant to subtle branch mutations.

targets.name: output-assembler
targets.rationale: The OUTPUT assembler is the schema-determined cut planner and serialiser behind the {frames + field-map} to JSON boundary. Its witness command includes unit, nested round-trip, documented nesting, v2 inference, and exact checkpoint-boundary contracts. The measured local survivor rate is 9.09% against the unchanged 10% ceiling after syntax-only annotation and keyword-marker exclusions; executable planner and assembly behavior remains in scope.

targets.name: jsonpath
targets.rationale: The single-sourced path-grammar core (PATH_GRAMMAR.md) — acceptance, canonicality, and the canonical writer. Both INPUT and OUTPUT depend on it, so subtle branch mutations are high-priority signal. Residual survivors are five equivalent mutants: '==' -> 'is' on single-char (interned) dispatch, '<' -> '!='/'is not' on a loop bound that never overshoots, and '==' -> '>=' on the canonical-writer round-trip (a canonical re-emit never lexically exceeds its input).

targets.name: json-shred
targets.rationale: The structured-input engine is the load-bearing JSON/JSONL/XML decomposition, bounded-spill, cache-publication, source-proof, cross-process-lock, and runtime-snapshot boundary. Its maintained 557-test mutation command combines seven focused hardening modules with 334 exact selectors that accounted for every named killer in the latest complete run; one 16-second integration witness is replaced by the new direct signature witnesses, while all broader modules remain in ordinary CI. It exercises parser conservation, multi-port loading, native source revisions, direct spill limits, atomic prepare/commit/discard, recovery, concurrent locking, source invalidation, process ownership, and adversarial cleanup paths. The isolated Windows baseline is 37.5 seconds in pytest and 40.1 seconds end to end under the unchanged 90-second ceiling. The 5% survival ceiling remains unchanged as the module grows. Only proven-equivalent selection and syntax-only postponed annotations are excluded with reviewed pragmas; executable expressions and branch decisions remain mutation-tested.

targets.name: json-cache
targets.rationale: The v2 per-port JSON cache route owns build/status/cancel/progress/infer/delete orchestration over the shred engine. Its 74-test cold-cache command contains every exact test that killed a route mutant in the latest complete run; the broader modules remain in ordinary CI. Focused witnesses cover path confinement, exact worker-manifest binding under adversarial equality overloads, native-memory diagnostics, progress reference counts and timing, response aggregation, and publication failures. The isolated Windows baseline is 32.2 seconds in pytest and 41.1 seconds end to end under the unchanged 60-second ceiling. The measured survivor rate is 8.56% against the unchanged 11% ceiling after syntax-only exclusions.

targets.name: executor
targets.rationale: The graph executor runs live Polars pipelines across preview, projection, materialisation, caching, sandboxed code, and transactional outputs. The maintained witnesses cover resource defaults, prepared-output immutability, path confinement, preamble safety, preview budgets, cache completeness, graph execution, model scoring, tracing, and output publication. Syntax-only postponed annotations and keyword markers are excluded; executable decisions remain under the unchanged 15% ceiling.

targets.name: parser-conservation
targets.rationale: The parser's structural acceptance gate is the F3 boundary (ENG-T07): it rejects any parse that lost an authored node, edge, handle or submodel reference, and reports a parent connection to a definition-owned child as dangling instead of dropping it. Its witness command is the conservation suite alone (34 tests, 3.4 seconds per run on the 2026-09-06 Windows baseline; 170 mutants before exclusions). Syntax-only postponed annotations are excluded with reviewed pragmas; the direct gate tests kill every comparison mutant on the node, edge and submodel-path mismatch branches. A fresh run of the committed gate and tests on 2026-09-06 left 3 effective survivors of 170 (1.76%). Residual survivors are three equivalent mutants: 'count > 1' -> 'count != 1' on Counter values that are never zero, 'pair[0] != target' -> 'is not' on interned identifiers, and 'root_ids | aliases' -> '^' on disjoint id sets.
